title: Cannot deduce generic type of bound TypeVar through Type of Union
body:
**Bug Report**

Inspired as a follow-up to [this StackOverflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70840506/how-to-pass-union-typed-values-to-generic-function-without-isinstance/70844389#70844389), I believe that mypy cannot deduce a generic type of a bound `TypeVar` through `Type` of a `Union` - it seems to deduce `object` in all cases and I'm not sure why.

```python3
from typing import TypeVar, Type, Callable, Union, Any

# t1 is a non-union type
t1: Type[bool] = bool
# t2 is a union type
t2: Union[Type[bool], Type[str]] = bool

# T1 is bound by a single Union type (supertype of bool and str)
T1 = TypeVar("T1", bound=Union[bool, str])
def foo1(t: Type[T1]) -> None: ...
foo1(t1)  # pass
foo1(t2)  # error: Value of type variable "T1" of "foo1" cannot be "object"

# T2 is bound by multiple types
T2 = TypeVar("T2", bool, str)
def foo2(t: Type[T2]) -> None: ...
foo2(t1)  # pass
foo2(t2)  # error: Value of type variable "T2" of "foo2" cannot be "object"
# note that this wouldn't work anyway as T2 cannot be Union[bool, str]

# T3 is not bound (can bind to object)
T3 = TypeVar("T3")
def foo3(t: Type[T3]) -> None: ...
foo3(t1)  # pass
foo3(t2)  # pass

# Shows that type deduction deduces Union when not using Type
# T1 = TypeVar("T1", bound=Union[bool, str])
def foo4(t: T1) -> None: ...
t3: bool = True
t4: Union[bool, str] = False
foo4(t3)  # pass
foo4(t4)  # pass

# Shows that type checking works when not using TypeVars, suggesting a problem
# with type deduction specifically
def foo5(t: Type[Union[bool, str]]) -> None: ...
foo5(t1)  # pass
foo5(t2)  # pass

```

**To Reproduce**

https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=latest&python=3.10&gist=a3423ef3aed84424b9e9d295cf19d41b

**Expected Behavior**

This is not rigorous, but I would expect that mypy could "figure out" that a value of `Union[Type[bool], Type[str]]` can satisfy the bound of `Union[bool, str]` for `T` in the expression `Type[T]`.

Am I misunderstanding something about the relationships between these types? Should this work?

Thanks for any insight.
